name: readiness_missing_signals_reweight
why: Partial logging must still produce a score by proportional reweighting, never by treating missing as zero. The reweighting is invisible to the user — the screen is the ordinary Today screen with a lower score.

given.formula_note: present weights sleep .25, energy .15 (of the .90 that the 8 user-loggable signals carry) renormalize to .5625/.3375; sleep=75, energy=25; all other USER-LOGGABLE signals absent (their weight redistributed among the present loggable signals). Training load is never absent and is never reweighted away: with no sessions yesterday it scores 100 (full recovery, PRD R2) and keeps its fixed .10. score=round(.5625*75+.3375*25+.10*100)=round(60.625)=61.

expect.counts_universe: reweighting spans the 8 user-loggable signals. Training load (R2's ninth) is derived from yesterday's sessions, has no log tile, and is never reweighted away — with no sessions it scores 100.
render_properties: the screen is the ordinary Today screen — same layout, lower score, amber band
no notice, banner or badge announces that signals are missing (PRD R4)

revision.why: The original arithmetic dropped training load entirely (.625/.375 sum to 1 with no load term), contradicting this fixture's own prose ('never absent', 'never reweighted away'), PRD R2 ('always present') and fixture 01 (load carries .10). The rule implemented — the 8 loggable weights (.90) renormalize among the signals present; load keeps its fixed .10 — satisfies every sentence of the prose and reproduces fixture 01 exactly. Only the number changed. Band stays yellow.
